answer: In an agent marketplace trading saffron grown on meadow farms, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid for jobs, and each bond permits only one active bid. A spiral of fake accounts therefore cannot multiply bids for free: 1,000 identities require $100,000 locked up. The defense does not prove identities are unique; it makes buying extra bidding capacity consume capital and incur financing costs.
